sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on Major highways and arterials in Lincoln or surface streets in Lincoln can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.

sections.heading: Lincoln documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. Lincoln insurers expect timestamped photos.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: Lincoln has Lincoln area hospitals and emergency departments among its major facilities. Verify the nearest trauma center if injuries may be serious.

sections.heading: Nebraska reporting rules
paragraphs: Nebraska requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 25/50/25.
Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through the investigating agency. If police do not respond, check https://dot.nebraska.gov/ for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
Nebraska uses 51% bar comparative negligence; anything you say can affect fault allocation.

paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near High-traffic corridors in Lincoln, NE is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
